text:
maya: Quick proposal — I'd like to add an interactive preflight flow to deploy-bot that walks the releaser through a short checklist, optional version pinning reason, and a release-note draft. keeps humans in the loop for risky changes.

chris: sounds useful. UX idea? inline prompts or open a modal? :thinking_face:

maya: start simple: inline interactive prompts in the thread + prompts to open the release-note template if requested. example command:
```
/deploy --env=prod --model=rwd-v3 --interactive
```
This would run the usual preflight checks and then ask: "Confirm DB migrations applied? (y/n)", "Pin version? (y/n)" and allow a one-line pin reason.

samuel: +1. Important: store the pin reason and who confirmed in the audit log. Also add a flag --pin-reason to be used non-interactively for automation.

liz: two questions: 1) how does this play with existing templates and CI (we don't want duplicate release notes) 2) can we gate the interactive flow behind change-windows for big infra changes?

maya: answers — 1) interactive flow would create a draft release note in /releases/drafts/<deploy_ts>.md and optionally push a comment with the link. CI can opt-out with --ci. 2) yes, default behavior: if the change touches infra or model-major (major version bump), require confirmation during the change window or require an override token from eng-oncall.

tao: propose a small release note template we can default to, so people don't have to invent one every time:
```
- What changed (1 line):
- Why (1-2 lines):
- Risk & mitigations:
- Rollback plan:
```
Also propose a --dry-run-interactive that walks prompts but doesn't actually toggle traffic, for rehearsals.

chris: we should also surface a memory/cost estimate in the interactive preflight (how many GPUs, expected peak mem, estimated tokens/sec) so releasers know impact. dry-run should show the planned kernel config and batching suggestions.

deploy-bot: interactive preflight started for /deploy by maya at 1768004567.
Checks run: model artifact checksum ✓, container build ✓, infra lint ✗ (1 warning), canary config ✓.
Prompt: "Confirm DB migrations applied? (y/n)"

samuel: for rollback policy, suggest default: auto-rollback if error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m OR latency regression +50% for 3m. still allow manual override. store metric thresholds in project config.

maya: agreed. Also want the bot to auto-open a minimal postmortem template when rollback occurs, prefilled with the deploy ID and metrics snapshot. reduces friction.

liz: edge case: if someone accidentally pins an older model, we need a safe unpin + pin-forward flow with approval. maybe require two approvals for pinning to old tags.

chris: add a quick command: `/deploy undo-pin --deploy-id=<id> --reason="typo"` that warns and requires second approver ack.

maya: implementation plan (rough):
- phase 1: interactive prompts + --pin-reason + store audit log + draft release-note linking (2 weeks)
- phase 2: dry-run interactive + memory/cost estimate + canary checks surfaced (3 weeks)
- phase 3: change-window enforcement, override tokens, two-approver pin flows (2 weeks)

tao: can help with release template and draft storage. I'll prototype the modal and a small RFC for approval flows.

deploy-bot: note — will emit structured deploy metadata to /audit/deploys.json and post a thread summary when flow completes.

maya: ok let's start with a thin MVP (phase 1). @chris @samuel can you review the PR when I open it? :thumbsup:

chris: yep, will review.

samuel: I'll add the audit storage schema.

liz: calling out operations: please remind eng-oncall about override tokens once implemented.

maya: thanks everyone — I'll draft a short release plan and open a PR with the interactive handler tomorrow. :rocket:
